stories.title: aggregate_combined helper in dataset_registry.py
acceptanceCriteria: dataset_registry.py exports aggregate_combined(per_dataset: dict[str, float], method: str = 'geometric', floor: float = 0.01) -> dict
method supports: 'geometric', 'mean', 'min'
Returns dict with keys: combined, combined_mean, combined_min, per_dataset
Geometric mean uses max(v, floor) per value to avoid zero-collapse
Inline self-test in __main__: for input {'s': 0.738, 'k': 0.25, 'e': 0.05} with method='geometric' + floor=0.01, returned combined is within 0.001 of hand-computed value (≈ 0.227)
Self-test also covers method='mean' and method='min'

stories.title: DSP single-position accessors — phase_z_at / t2_z_at / cpe_z_at
acceptanceCriteria: detector.py exposes `phase_z_at(chunk_ctx, t_sec) -> float`, `t2_z_at(chunk_ctx, t_sec) -> float`, `cpe_z_at(chunk_ctx, t_sec) -> float` that return the chunk-local z-score at a given time without re-running the full detection pipeline
A new `_build_chunk_context(chunk, sr) -> dict` precomputes phase/T2/CPE curves once per chunk so the per-t accessors are O(1) lookups
The existing detect_splices code path still works unchanged (accessors are additive; current API preserved)

Sanity: uv run python -c "from detector import _build_chunk_context, phase_z_at, t2_z_at, cpe_z_at; import librosa; y,sr=librosa.load('data/spliced/tier1/splice_t1_001.wav', sr=None); ctx=_build_chunk_context(y[:60*sr], sr); print(phase_z_at(ctx, 30.0), t2_z_at(ctx, 30.0), cpe_z_at(ctx, 30.0))" returns three floats without error

stories.title: 15-cell metric aggregator + FP multiplier
acceptanceCriteria: dataset_registry.py adds `forensic_combined(per_cell: dict[str, float], clean_fp: int, max_allowed: int, floor: float = 0.01) -> dict` that computes geometric mean of the 15 cells (floored) × (1 - clean_fp/max_allowed) clamped to [0, 1]
Cell names follow convention `<dataset>_t<tier>_<regime>` for 12 spliced cells and `<dataset>_clean_score` for 3 clean cells
Returns dict with keys: combined, combined_gm_cells, fp_multiplier, per_cell, n_cells_included

Inline __main__ test: for 15 synthetic cells all at 0.5 + 0 clean_fp, combined == 0.5. For one cell at 0.01 + others at 0.5, combined drops below 0.38 (demonstrating GM penalty). For 5 clean_fp / max_allowed=15, fp_multiplier == 0.667.
Does NOT replace the existing aggregate_combined — it sits alongside as the forensic-specific aggregator

stories.title: Feature extraction module features.py (~66 dims per candidate)
acceptanceCriteria: New features.py at repo root exports `extract_features(audio, sr, t_sec, chunk_ctx=None) -> dict[str, float]` returning ~66 named features
Feature categories covered: 4 DSP scores, 13 MFCC pre/post deltas, 6 spectral summary deltas, 6 noise-floor color features, 8 pitch/voicing, 6 energy/ZCR, 3 boundary-region, 20 mel-PCA-tail
Every feature has a documented name; `extract_features` also exports FEATURE_NAMES list for SHAP labeling
Idempotent: same (audio, sr, t) produces identical output vector
Performance: 1000 calls on a cached chunk_ctx complete in <2s on laptop CPU (budget for dense scanning)
Integration: ml_eval or a training script can call it to produce a feature matrix
Note: PCA fit for mel tail is pre-loaded from a training-time fit file if present; self-fit fallback if not

stories.title: Multi-class GBM training pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: .omc/classifier/train_classifier.py trains a 3-class GBM (not_splice / hard_cut / crossfade) using features.py output

Training data: for each spliced file, label positive candidates (within 1s of GT) by tier (1→hard_cut, 2→crossfade); label negatives sampled from both spliced (far from GT) and clean files as not_splice
GroupKFold by file_id preserved; OOF multi-class F1 reported (weighted and per-class)
Saved joblib artifact at .omc/classifier/fp_classifier.joblib works with `model.predict_proba([features_vector])` returning shape (1, 3)
Multi-class OOF F1 (weighted) ≥ 0.70 on training distribution (softer than binary 0.85 because 3-way is harder; ground-truth target)

stories.title: Detector refactor — GBM-first dense scan
acceptanceCriteria: detector.py `detect_splices` replaces DSP-first logic with: slide chunks (W=60s, S=50s); for each chunk call `_build_chunk_context` then `gbm.predict_proba` at every candidate position (stride = ANALYSIS_STRIDE_S = 0.2s); emit (t, label, probability) when p_splice > THRESHOLD (default 0.5)
Labels are 'hard_cut' or 'crossfade' from argmax of the two non-not_splice classes
Memoization cache preserved (keyed by audio fingerprint + model hash so it invalidates when the classifier changes)
DIAG observability preserved — existing DIAG lines for GPD unfit / hotelling near-singular still emit; one new DIAG emits per chunk with (scan_count, emit_count)
Sliding window geometry (W=60, S=50) unchanged
Existing eval_by_regime.py works without modification (same API: `detect_splices(audio, sr) -> list[float]` with times in file coordinates)
